skill.name: doc-coauthoring
skill.description: Guides users through a structured workflow for writing documentation, proposals, technical specs, and decision documents.
skill.summary: Co-author structured documents through context gathering, section drafting, iterative refinement, and reader testing.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

The hardcoded URL and reconnaissance findings are benign guidance for manual Claude testing and user-authorized context sharing. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: The line uses markdown backticks around the tool name create_file, not Ruby or shell execution. It instructs document scaffolding, with no dynamic command string.
The backticks wrap example filenames in documentation prose. No shell command or executable interpolation is present.
The line names str_replace as an editing tool inside markdown. It does not execute code or pass user text to a shell.
The line uses markdown backticks for the editing tool name str_replace. It is guidance for targeted document edits, not command execution.
The backticked create_file text is a tool reference in an artifact management checklist. It is not a shell command or Ruby backtick expression.
The backticked str_replace text is a tool reference in prose. There is no executable command, interpolation, or hidden process launch.
The URL is the public Claude.ai site used for manual reader testing. The skill tells the user to open it themselves, not to make a hidden network request.
The cited lines offer user-selected ways to provide writing context, such as a stream-of-consciousness dump or links. They do not instruct network scanning or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Complex documents often fail when readers lack the author's context. This skill guides context gathering, section drafting, iterative edits, and reader testing.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through context gathering questions for documentation projects.
Builds document structures with placeholders for agreed sections.
Brainstorms section content and helps curate which points to keep.
Drafts and refines sections using targeted edits.
Supports reader testing with sub-agents or manual fresh Claude checks.
Checks final documents for flow, redundancy, contradictions, and generic filler.
limitations: Requires users to supply source context or grant connector access.
Cannot verify facts, links, or technical claims without available evidence.
Manual reader testing is required when sub-agents are not available.
May handle sensitive organizational context, so users must avoid sharing restricted information.

use_cases.title: Create a technical spec
use_cases.description: Turn architecture context, constraints, and trade-offs into a structured spec that engineers can review.

use_cases.title: Draft a decision document
use_cases.description: Capture options, reasoning, and expected impact before asking stakeholders to align on a decision.

use_cases.title: Prepare a proposal
use_cases.description: Build a persuasive proposal from raw context, then test whether readers understand the request.

prompt_templates.title: Start a documentation workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write a technical spec for [project]. Ask me the context questions needed before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Turn raw context into sections
prompt_templates.prompt: I need a proposal for [audience]. Use this context dump and suggest the best document structure: [context].

prompt_templates.title: Refine a section with feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise the [section name] section. Keep points [list], remove [list], and make the tone more direct.

prompt_templates.title: Run reader testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the current document to predict reader questions, test for ambiguity, and recommend targeted fixes.

output_examples.input: Draft a decision document from context about replacing an internal deployment process.
output_examples.output: A section-by-section outline with placeholders, followed by focused questions about audience, risks, alternatives, and success criteria.

output_examples.input: Improve the technical approach section after stakeholder feedback.
output_examples.output: A targeted revision plan that keeps selected points, removes duplicated material, and proposes concise replacement text.

output_examples.input: Test whether a fresh reader would understand the proposal.
output_examples.output: A reader-testing report that lists likely questions, ambiguous assumptions, contradictions, and recommended document edits.

best_practices: Provide raw context early, including constraints, trade-offs, and audience expectations.
Review each drafted section before moving to the next one.
Run reader testing before sharing important documents with stakeholders.
anti_patterns: Do not skip context gathering for documents with complex decisions.
Do not paste restricted company data unless your policy allows it.
Do not accept generic filler when a section needs concrete evidence.

faq.question: What document types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports technical specs, proposals, decision documents, RFCs, PRDs, and similar structured documents.

faq.question: Does it write the whole document at once?
faq.answer: No. It guides section-by-section drafting so each part can be reviewed and refined.

faq.question: Can it use team channels or shared documents?
faq.answer: Yes, when approved integrations are available and the user directs it to use them.

faq.question: What is reader testing?
faq.answer: Reader testing checks whether a fresh Claude conversation can understand the document without prior context.

faq.question: Does it verify factual accuracy?
faq.answer: It can flag claims that need verification, but users must check facts, links, and technical details.

faq.question: Is it suitable for sensitive documents?
faq.answer: Use it only with information you are allowed to share with the selected AI tool and connectors.
